- Critical: DELETE /admin/users/:id has no requireUser middleware, so it is unauthenticated. /reports/sales only checks that a valid token exists, with no role check. Async handlers have no try/catch, so rejected promises are unhandled unless express handles them. Req.body fields are passed unvalidated.
- Summary: Express router for the shop API with four routes: login, order placement, sales report, and admin user deletion. Only orders and reports use requireUser.

## auth
- Files: auth.js
- Functions: login(email, password) (exported async; returns token or null), issueToken(userId) (exported; signs JWT with config.jwtSecret), verifyToken(token) (exported; returns decoded payload or null, does not throw)
- Dependencies: auth -> config.js (jwtSecret, sessionTtlMinutes) -> auth -> database.js (query) -> api-routes -> auth.js (login, verifyToken)
- Critical: verifyToken returns null instead of throwing, so requireUser's catch never runs and requests with an invalid token pass with req.user = null. This breaks auth on /orders and /reports/sales. login builds SQL by string concatenation (SQL injection). Passwords are checked with unsalted MD5. sessionTtlMinutes is passed as jwt expiresIn, which is interpreted as seconds.
- Summary: Handles login with password hash check and JWT issue and verification. Contains SQL injection, weak MD5 hashing, and a verifyToken that fails open to null.

- Dependencies: cart -> config.js (maxCartItems)
- Critical: addItem does not validate quantity; zero or negative quantities are accepted, and a negative quantity can reduce or make a line total negative. The full-cart check counts lines, not units. Nothing here checks that priceCents comes from trusted catalog data, so callers must supply it safely. Callers of cartTotal depend on this trust boundary."
- Summary: Simple in-memory cart with integer-cent totals. Merges lines by SKU and enforces a max line count, but does not validate quantity or price.

- Critical: sessionTtlMinutes is 30 but auth.js passes it to jwt expiresIn, which treats numbers as seconds, so tokens live 30 seconds. jwtSecret and databaseUrl come from env with no fallback or startup check, so they may be undefined. Comment says minutes, so the unit mismatch is a real bug.

- Files: database.js

- Critical: query does not release the connection if connection.query throws, so a failed statement leaks a pool client. Parameters are passed through but callers can still build raw SQL strings, as auth.js login does. Pool is created at import time using config.databaseUrl, which may be undefined.
- Summary: Shared PostgreSQL access layer with a single query helper that returns rows and rowCount, plus closePool for shutdown.

## inventory
- Files: inventory.js
- Functions: stockLevel(sku) (exported async; intended to return quantity or 0), reserveStock(sku, quantity) (exported async; checks stockLevel, decrements stock, returns { sku, reserved })
- Dependencies: inventory -> database.js (query) -> inventory.js is used by order placement (orders.js, not yet confirmed in this review)

No check that quantity is positive."
- Summary: Stock lookup and reservation. stockLevel is broken by a wrong destructuring of query results, and reserveStock does not await its update, so reservations can be lost and oversold.

## auth
- Files: auth.js
- Functions: login(email, password), issueToken(userId), verifyToken(token)
- Dependencies: auth.js -> config.js (jwtSecret, sessionTtlMinutes) -> auth.js -> database.js (query) -> api-routes.js -> auth.js (login, verifyToken)
- Critical: verifyToken returns null on failure instead of throwing. Because requireUser in api-routes.js only catches exceptions, an invalid token yields req.user = null and next() is still called. Authentication is therefore not enforced on POST /orders or GET /reports/sales; POST /orders then throws on req.user.id. DELETE /admin/users/:id has no middleware at all.
- Summary: Login and JWT session module. login() builds SQL by string concatenation (SQL injection via email) and checks passwords with unsalted MD5. issueToken() signs {id} with config.jwtSecret and expiresIn set from sessionTtlMinutes (jsonwebtoken treats a bare number as seconds, so the unit is likely wrong). verifyToken() returns the payload or null and never throws.

## api-routes
- Files: api-routes.js
- Functions: router (express.Router: POST /login, POST /orders, GET /reports/sales, DELETE /admin/users/:id)
- Dependencies: api-routes.js -> auth.js (login, verifyToken) -> api-routes.js -> orders.js (placeOrder) -> api-routes.js -> reports.js (salesReport) -> api-routes.js -> users.js (deleteUser)
- Critical: Auth is broken on the routes that use requireUser (/orders, /reports/sales), and DELETE /admin/users/:id has no middleware. POST /login reads req.body fields without validation. Async handlers have no try/catch, so Express 4 will not forward rejections. Earlier scratchpad said requireUser returns 401 on failure; that was wrong.
- Summary: Express routes for the shop API. Only export is router. Internal helper requireUser(req, res, next) sets req.user from verifyToken and calls next(). Corrected from prior note: requireUser never returns 401 for a bad token, because verifyToken returns null rather than throwing, so the try/catch never fires.

## cart
- Files: cart.js
- Functions: createCart(), addItem(cart, item), cartTotal(cart)
- Dependencies: cart.js -> config.js (maxCartItems)
- Critical: addItem does not validate item.quantity or item.priceCents; negative, zero, or non-integer values are accepted, so a negative quantity could reduce cartTotal. The maxCartItems check counts distinct lines, not total units. Callers must validate input.
- Summary: In-memory shopping cart with integer-cent pricing. createCart() returns { items: [] }. addItem() throws "Cart is full" when line count reaches config.maxCartItems, merges quantity for an existing SKU, otherwise pushes a copy of the item. cartTotal() sums priceCents * quantity. No auth or SQL involvement.

## config
- Files: config.js
- Functions: config (exported object: databaseUrl, jwtSecret, sessionTtlMinutes, vatRate, maxCartItems, mailFrom)
- Dependencies: config.js is imported by auth.js (jwtSecret, sessionTtlMinutes), cart.js (maxCartItems), and likely database.js (databaseUrl) and orders.js (vatRate, mailFrom)
- Critical: jwtSecret and databaseUrl are read from environment variables with no fallback; if unset they are undefined and nothing here fails fast. sessionTtlMinutes is 30 but issueToken passes it to jsonwebtoken as expiresIn, which treats a bare number as seconds, so tokens last 30 seconds rather than 30 minutes unless auth.js converts units.
- Summary: Static application settings module. Secrets (DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET) come from the environment. Other values are hardcoded: session TTL 30 minutes, VAT 0.19, max 50 cart lines, and a mailFrom address. Exports a single `config` object. No functions and no logic.

## database
- Files: database.js
- Functions: query(sql, params = []) -> Promise<{ rows, rowCount }>, closePool() -> Promise<void>
- Dependencies: database.js -> config.js (databaseUrl) -> auth.js -> database.js (query) -> database.js is the shared data-access layer; other modules should call query()
- Critical: query() supports parameterized params, but auth.js login() builds SQL by string concatenation and bypasses them (SQL injection risk). query() does not release the pooled connection if connection.query throws, so failed queries leak clients from the pool; a try/finally is needed. pool is created at import time using config.databaseUrl, which may be undefined.
- Summary: Thin wrapper around a pg.Pool. query() checks out a connection, runs one parameterized statement, releases the connection, and returns { rows, rowCount }. closePool() ends the pool. No other exports.

## inventory
- Files: inventory.js
- Functions: stockLevel(sku) -> Promise<number>, reserveStock(sku, quantity) -> Promise<{ sku, reserved }>
- Dependencies: inventory.js -> database.js (query) -> inventory.js has no importers found yet; check orders.js for reserveStock callers
- Critical: stockLevel destructures `const [row] = await query(...)`, but database.js query() returns { rows, rowCount } (per prior notes), which is not iterable, so this likely throws a TypeError; it should use `.rows[0]`. reserveStock calls query() for the UPDATE without await or return, so the write is fire-and-forget: failures become unhandled rejections and the caller is told the reservation succeeded. The check-then-update is also a race (TOCTOU) between stockLevel and the UPDATE, with no transaction or row lock. quantity is not validated, so a negative value increases stock.

- Functions: sendOrderEmail(user, order) -> Promise<void>
- Dependencies: notifications.js -> config.js (mailFrom) -> notifications.js -> utils.js (formatCurrency) -> notifications.js -> mailer-stub.js (mailer.send)
- Critical: user.name is interpolated into HTML without escaping (HTML injection). The try/catch around mailer.send is empty, so send failures are silently swallowed and the caller never learns the email failed. formatCurrency is passed order.total with no stated unit (cents vs. euros is unverified against cart.js, which uses integer cents).
- Summary: Sends the customer order-confirmation email. Builds HTML from user.name and a formatted order.total, then calls mailer.send with config.mailFrom. Only export is sendOrderEmail. No importers checked yet.

## orders

- Dependencies: orders.js -> cart.js (cartTotal) -> orders.js -> config.js (taxRate) -> orders.js -> database.js (query) -> orders.js -> inventory.js (reserveStock) -> orders.js -> notifications.js (sendOrderEmail) -> orders.js -> payments.js (chargeCard) -> orders.js -> users.js (findUserById) -> api-routes.js -> orders.js (placeOrder)

- Summary: Order placement module. orderTax() computes tax with Math.round(netCents * config.taxRate). placeOrder() reserves stock per cart line, computes cartTotal, charges the card via payments.js, inserts an orders row, sends a confirmation email, and returns { id, total, tax }. Note: the tax is applied to total, which is the same value passed as the net amount, so it is unclear whether total is net or gross.

## payments
- Files: payments.js
- Functions: chargeCard(card, amountEuros) -> Promise<{ id }>, refundCharge(chargeId) -> Promise<boolean>
